Blepahroplasty Quiz

What is Upper Blepharoplasty?

Upper blepharoplasty is a surgical procedure designed to correct issues with the upper eyelids. This surgery targets and removes excess skin, muscle, and sometimes fat from the upper eyelids, resulting in a smoother and more lifted appearance. Upper blepharoplasty effectively eliminates droopy upper eyelids, improving both your vision and aesthetic appeal.

The Upper Eyelid Lift Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons utilize advanced techniques to ensure the best possible outcomes for upper blepharoplasty. During the procedure, an incision is made along the natural crease of the upper eyelid. Through this incision, excess skin, muscle, and sometimes fat are removed or repositioned to create a smoother and more lifted contour. The incision is then carefully closed, resulting in minimal scarring that is typically well-hidden within the natural folds of the eyelid.

Healing and Outcomes

Recovery from upper eyelid surgery is generally smooth, with most patients experiencing mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Cold compresses and prescribed medications can help manage these symptoms. Most patients return to their normal activities within 10-14 days. The final results, which can be seen as swelling subsides, include a more youthful and rejuvenated appearance with improved eyelid function.

Frequently Asked Questions | Upper Eyelid Lift Surgery

What Issues Does Upper Eyelid Surgery Address?

Upper blepharoplasty targets the sagging, excess skin, muscle, and sometimes fat on the upper eyelids, improving both the aesthetic appearance and functional vision.

Can My Insurance Cover This Procedure?

While upper eyelid lifts are typically considered cosmetic and not covered by insurance, there are instances where the procedure might be covered if it is performed to improve obstructed vision or address a medical condition.

Who Should Consider an Upper Eyelid Lift?

Ideal candidates for upper eyelid lift surgery are individuals with droopy or sagging upper eyelids affecting their vision or appearance, who are in good overall health.

What Can I Expect During Recovery?

Post-surgery recovery generally takes about 10-14 days, with most swelling and bruising diminishing during this period. Full results are typically visible as the remaining swelling subsides over a few months.

Are There Risks Involved with This Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

What Kind of Results Can I Anticipate?

You can expect a more youthful and refreshed look with reduced sagging and drooping of the upper eyelids. Additionally, your vision may improve if drooping eyelids were previously obstructing your view.
